LEO2CILICIA.name: Leo II of Cilician Armenia
LEO2CILICIA.summary: Son of Hetum I and Elizabeth, he was held captive after the Mamluk invasion of 1266. As king he continued to seek Mongolian support against Egypt. His numerous offspring linked Armenia with Byzantium and the Lusignan.

MARIAANABAVIERA.name: Maria Ana of Bavaria
MARIAANABAVIERA.summary: Consort of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Their life is linked to Inner Austria.

MATILDAING.name: Matilde of England
MATILDAING.summary: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their life is linked to Saxony, England.

RUXANDRARARES.name: Ruxandra Rareș
RUXANDRARARES.summary: The daughter of Petru Rareș and Elena Branković, she married Alejandro Lăpușneanu. She intervened in the continuity of her family and, after the removal and death of her husband, exercised the regency of Bogdan IV. Her ancestry links the Moldovan sovereigns with the family of the Serbian despots.

CRISTINASUE.name: Christina of Sweden
CRISTINASUE.summary: Queen of Sweden and daughter of Gustavus Adolphus, she was renowned for her intellectual and cultural interests. She abdicated in 1654, converted to Catholicism and spent much of her life in Rome.
sections: Daughter of Gustavo II Adolfo and Maria Leonor of Brandenburg, born in Stockholm in 1626 and inherited the throne in 1632. She was educated as an heir prince and ruled a regency presided over by Chancellor Oxenstierna until her majority in 1644.
Westphalia and the Court of Stockholm

He promoted the peace of Westphalia (1648), which gave Sweden Western Pomerania, Bremen and Verden. He brought wise men and artists, including René Descartes, to Stockholm, who died there in 1650. He refused to marry and managed to get the Riksdag to recognize his cousin Carlos Gustavo as heir.

In 1654 he abdicated in it and became secret to Catholicism, making it public in Innsbruck in 1655. He settled in Rome, where he protected musicians such as Corelli and Alessandro Scarlatti and gathered notable collections. He unsuccessfully tried to obtain the crown of Naples and that of Poland. He died in Rome in 1689 and is buried in St. Peter.

governmentNotes.Autoridad superior de las fuerzas de ocu: Superior authority over the Swedish occupation forces. The municipal history documents military occupation from 1642 to 1650. Christina is the Swedish sovereign during this period; military command and administration belong to her officers. She receives no margravial title and is not assigned all Moravia.

EMANUELFILIBERTOSAB.name: Emmanuel Philibert of Savoy
EMANUELFILIBERTOSAB.summary: He inherited a duchy occupied largely by other powers. His service to Charles V and Philip II, and especially the victory of San Quintin, contributed to the territorial recovery agreed at Cateau-Cambresis.
EMANUELFILIBERTOSAB.biography: He inherited a duchy occupied largely by other powers. His service to Charles V and Philip II, and especially the victory of Saint Quintin, contributed to the territorial recovery agreed upon in Cateau-Cambrésis. He moved the capital to Turin and married Margaret of France. His title of 1553 and the effective recovery of 1559 represented different moments.

ISABELLEFOIX.name: Isabel de Foix-Castellbó
ISABELLEFOIX.summary: He inherited the rights of his brother Matthew and was the figure who sustained Foix's patrimonial continuity by passing to the descendants of the Grailly. Her husband Archambaud participated in the government for that marriage.
ISABELLEFOIX.biography: He inherited the rights of his brother Matthew and was the figure who sustained Foix's patrimonial continuity by passing to the descendants of the Grailly. Her husband Archambaud participated in the government for that marriage. The distinction between the heiress and the consort allows to read correctly the origin of the Foix-Grailly line.

governmentNotes.Título conservado después de la transmis: Title retained after the transfer of government to John I.
governmentNotes.Título conservado tras transmitir el gob: Title retained after transferring government to John I.

LUISSAB.name: Luis de Savoy
LUISSAB.summary: The son of Amadeus VIII and Mary of Burgundy, he assumed government functions before becoming Duke. His marriage to Anna of Lusignan linked Savoy to Cyprus.
LUISSAB.biography: The son of Amadeus VIII and Mary of Burgundy, he assumed government functions before becoming Duke. His marriage to Anne of Lusignan linked Savoy to Cyprus. Among his sons were Dukes Amadeus IX and Philip II, besides Louis, who married Queen Charlotte of Cyprus and defended his cause on the island.

ISABELLALUSARM.name: Isabella of Armenia, wife of Amalric
aliases: Isabella of Armenia, Princess of Tyre
Zabel de Armenia, princesa de Tiro
ISABELLALUSARM.summary: Daughter of Leo II and Keran, she married Amalric of Lusignan. After the death of her husband, her family was caught up in the struggles of the Armenian court. Her descendants inherited the claim that led the Lusignans to the Cilician throne.

ANAAUSTRIAFRA.name: Anne of Austria
ANAAUSTRIAFRA.role: Queen consort and Regent of France
ANAAUSTRIAFRA.summary: Daughter of Philip III of Spain, wife of Louis XIII and mother of Louis XIV. Regent of France since 1643 with Cardinal Mazarino, crossed the Fronda without losing power.

INESANTIOQUIA.name: Agnes of Antioch
INESANTIOQUIA.summary: Consort of the Poitiers-Antioquia dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary.

JEANFOIXETAMPES.name: John of Foix, Viscount of Narbonne
JEANFOIXETAMPES.summary: The son of Gaston IV and Leonor of Navarre, he was the brother of Gaston, Prince of Viana, and uncle of Catherine of Navarre. He married Maria of Orleans. His sons Germana and Gaston of Nemours link this branch with the Aragonese court and with the French campaigns in Italy.

ISABELLA1JER.name: Isabella I of Jerusalem
ISABELLA1JER.summary: Queen of Jerusalem since 1190, daughter of Amalaric I. Her successive husbands, Conrad of Montferrato, Henry of Champagne and Amalric of Lusignan, ruled the kingdom with her.

AMEDEO5SAB.name: Amadeus V of Savoy
AMEDEO5SAB.summary: Son of Thomas II, he entered the county after the death of his uncle Philip I. His position was consolidated by agreements with other branches of the family, which retained their own rights. Edward and Aimon succeeded in Savoy; by their marriages, the count also linked with Bâgé and Brabant.

THOROS3ARM.name: Thoros III of Cilician Armenia
THOROS3ARM.summary: He received the throne after the withdrawal of his brother Hetum and later shared it with him. The dispute between brothers ended with his deposition and death in captivity. His son Leon regained the rights of his line.

FRANCISCO1TOSC.name: Francis I of Tuscany
FRANCISCO1TOSC.summary: His Tuscan government combined the interest in experimentation and the arts with a very personal court policy. The absence of a surviving male heir brought the great duchy to his brother Fernando.

JUAN3BRAB.name: John III of Brabant
JUAN3BRAB.summary: During the first half of the fourteenth century, he ruled Brabant and Limburg. His daughters Joanna and Margaret carried family rights along different paths. Joanna’s succession and Margaret’s Flemish marriage prepared the disputes and agreements that drew the duchy closer to the Burgundian lands.

LUISDELFIN1661.name: Louis, Grand Dauphin of France
LUISDELFIN1661.summary: The son of Louis XIV and heir of France, the Grand Dauphin. He died in 1711 before his father; his son Philip of Anjou was Philip V of Spain.

CONSTANZAARAGHUN.name: Constance of Aragon
CONSTANZAARAGHUN.summary: Consort of the Barcelona dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary, Holy Roman Empire, Aragon.

MARIAAUST.name: Mary of Austria
MARIAAUST.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary, the Netherlands.

VAKHTANG5KARTLI.name: Vajtang V de Kartli
VAKHTANG5KARTLI.summary: From Mukhrani, he was adopted as heir by Rostom and recognized by the Sah. He extended the influence of his family towards Kakheti and Imereti through his children. His trajectory combines Bagrationi legitimacy with the safavid investiture.

GIOVANNASABMON.name: Joan of Savoy, Marchioness of Montferrat
GIOVANNASABMON.summary: Daughter of Amadeus VII and Bona de Berry, she married Juan James of Montferrat. She was the mother of William VIII, Bonifacio III and Isabel, wife of Ludovico I of Saluzzo.
GIOVANNASABMON.biography: Daughter of Amadeus VII and Bona de Berry, she married Juan James of Montferrat. She was the mother of William VIII, Bonifacio III and Isabel, wife of Ludovico I of Saluzzo. Her position links several neighboring houses by filiation, but the alliances and conflicts of her descendants show that sharing ancestors did not guarantee political cooperation.

SIMON1KARTLI.name: Simon I of Kartli
SIMON1KARTLI.summary: He first fought the safavid intervention and spent years in captivity in Persia. Freed to fight the Ottomans, he re-ruled before falling prisoner to them. His two stages of government were separated so as not to present captivity as effective power.

MARIEEVREUXBRAB.name: Marie of Évreux, Duchess of Brabant
MARIEEVREUXBRAB.summary: The daughter of Louis de Évreux and Margaret of Artois, she married John III of Brabant. She was the mother of Joan of Brabant and Margaret, wife of Louis II of Flanders. Her offspring connect the Brabantine and Flemish successions with the Capetian branch of Évreux.

ESCLARFOIX.name: Esclaramunda of Foix
ESCLARFOIX.summary: Daughter of Roger IV of Foix, she married James II of Majorca. The union connected the Pyrenean house with a monarchy whose inheritance included both island and continental lands. Their descendants illustrate the Mediterranean reach of the Foix family.

MARIAANAAUTMAXBAV.name: Maria Ana of Austria
MARIAANAAUTMAXBAV.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life is linked to Austria, Bavaria.

ISABPI.name: Isabel Piast
ISABPI.summary: Consort of the Piast dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary.

CARLOS1ORLEANS.name: Charles I of Orleans
CARLOS1ORLEANS.summary: He was captured in Agincourt and spent many years in prison in England. His poetic work made him a prominent figure in French court literature.

JOHNLUSARM.name: Juan de Lusignan, regent of Armenia
aliases: John of Lusignan, regent of Armenia
JOHNLUSARM.summary: Son of Amalric and Elizabeth, he administered Armenia during the transition to the Lusignan monarchy and favored the candidacy of his brother Guido. His son Leon would be the last king to effectively rule the Cilician kingdom.

ERNSTCASIMIRNASSAU.name: Ernesto Casimiro de Nassau-Dietz
ERNSTCASIMIRNASSAU.summary: Count of Nassau, 1606–1632 (branch). Count of the Nassau dynasty.

governmentNotes.Cargo provincial delegado por los Estado: Provincial office delegated by the States, with individually documented dates and jurisdictions. Its scope excludes hereditary sovereignty over the whole Republic and the Spanish provinces.

FRED2SAX.name: Frederick II of Saxony
FRED2SAX.summary: Elector of Saxony since 1428, from the house of Wettin. He ruled with his brother Guillermo, with whom he fought the fratricidal Saxon war; his sons Ernesto and Alberto later divided the domains.

INESH.name: Inés de Habsburg
INESH.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary.

ISABARAGINF.name: Isabel of Aragon
ISABARAGINF.summary: Consort of the Trastámara dynasty. Their life is linked to Portugal, Castile, Aragon.

MARIALUISASABESP.name: María Luisa Gabriela de Savoy
MARIALUISASABESP.summary: Consort of the Savoy dynasty. Their life is linked to Spain, Savoy.

JOHN4BRAB.name: John IV of Brabant
JOHN4BRAB.summary: He inherited Brabant and married Jacqueline of Bavaria. The marriage drew him into the conflict over Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut, but did not permanently unite those inheritances. He was succeeded by his brother Philip of Saint-Pol.

DOROTHEALAUDEN.name: Dorothea of Saxony-Lauenburg
DOROTHEALAUDEN.summary: Consort of the Ascania dynasty. Their life is linked to Saxony-Lauenburg, Denmark.

ISABAUSTRIAPOL.name: Isabella of Austria
ISABAUSTRIAPOL.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life is linked to Poland, Austria.

MARGARETCYPARM.name: Margaret of Lusignan, Queen of Armenia
MARGARETCYPARM.summary: The daughter of Hugo III of Cyprus and wife of Theodore III of Armenia, she was the mother of Leo III. Her marriage is one of the direct links between the two monarchies, prior to the Lusignans' access to the Cilician crown.

EUPHEMIASUE.name: Eufemia of Sweden
EUPHEMIASUE.summary: Sister of Magnus Eriksson and daughter of Ingeborg of Norway. She married Albert II of Mecklenburg. Her son Albert was king of Sweden, while the offspring of his son Henry led to Erik of Pomerania. It is a key connection between Bjälbo, Mecklenburg and the Kalmar union.

YOLANDAARAG.name: Yolanda de Aragón
YOLANDAARAG.role: Queen consort and Regent of France
YOLANDAARAG.summary: Consort of the Barcelona dynasty. Their life is linked to Anjou, Aragon.

LEONALB.name: Leonor de Albuquerque
LEONALB.summary: Consort of the Trastámara dynasty. Their life is linked to Aragon, Castile.

TOMAS1SAB.name: Tomás I de Savoy
TOMAS1SAB.summary: He consolidated the Saudi domains on both sides of the Alps after a difficult minority. His offspring opened paths to the English and Provencal courts and to the Italian lordships.
TOMAS1SAB.biography: He consolidated the Saudi domains on both sides of the Alps after a difficult minority. His offspring opened paths to the English and Provencal courts and to the Italian lordships. The Condal succession followed Amadeus IV, but other children received their own patrimony and functions: belonging to the same house did not mean governing an undivided territory.

RITAARMENIA.name: Rita of Armenia
RITAARMENIA.summary: Consort of the Hethumid dynasty. Their life is linked to Cilician Armenia, Byzantium.

CHIAJNARARES.name: Chiajna Rareș
CHIAJNARARES.summary: Daughter of Petru Rareș and his first wife Maria, she married Mircea Ciobanul. After her husband’s death she directed the government of her son Petru. His deposition in 1568 drove the family into exile. She is still recorded in 1587, but the precise year of her death is unknown.

governmentNotes.Gobierno de su hijo Petru bajo la direcc: His son Petru's Government under his mother's political leadership, also after his first minority.

INGEBORGERIKNOR.name: Ingeborg of Denmark, Queen of Norway
INGEBORGERIKNOR.summary: Daughter of Erik IV of Denmark and wife of Magnus VI of Norway. She was mother of kings Erik II and Haakon V. After Magnus' death she participated in the government during the Erik minority, in a context of tensions between the crown, the aristocracy and the Church.

GIORGI2IMER.name: George II of Imereti
GIORGI2IMER.summary: He ruled between conflicts with the princes of Mingrelia and Guria and with growing Ottoman pressure. His sons and nephews would compete for a crown whose power depended increasingly on aristocratic alliances.

BLANCANAV.name: Blanca de Navarra
BLANCANAV.summary: Daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she married Philip VI of France. The marriage brought the Navarrese house into close connection with the first generation of Valois rulers.
BLANCANAV.biography: The daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she married Philip VI of France. This marriage brought the Navarrese house closer to the first generation of the Valois. Her trajectory allows us to distinguish this Blanca from other homonyms of Navarre belonging to different generations and successor situations.

ALONSARAG.name: Alonso de Aragón
ALONSARAG.summary: Archbishop of the Trastámara dynasty. Their life is linked to Aragon.

MARGLUX.name: Margarita de Luxembourg
MARGLUX.summary: Consort of the Luxembourg dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary.

CONST2ARM.name: Constantine II of Cilician Armenia
aliases: Guy de Lusignan, King of Armenia
CONST2ARM.summary: Born Guido de Lusignan, he accepted the crown after the death of his cousin Leo IV. His project of approach to the Latin Church found resistance among the nobles. He was murdered, putting an end to the first Lusignan reign in Cilicia.

GUGL8MON.name: William VIII of Montferrat
GUGL8MON.summary: The son of Juan Jacobo and Juana de Savoy, combined the government of Montferrat with the military service of the Italian powers. His daughters married Ludovico II of Saluzzo and Charles I of Savoy.
GUGL8MON.biography: The son of Juan Jacobo and Juana de Savoy combined the government of Montferrat with the military service of the Italian powers. His daughters married Ludovico II of Saluzzo and Carlos I of Savoy. These links generated expectations about the marquisado, but upon his death his brother Bonifacio III inherited it.

LEONORPROVENZA.name: Leonor de Provence
LEONORPROVENZA.summary: Consort of the Barcelona dynasty. Their life is linked to England.

DEMETRIO2GEO.name: Demetrius II of Georgia
DEMETRIO2GEO.summary: He reigned in eastern Georgia under the Iljanate and participated in his campaigns. His execution by order of the Khan illustrates how far the sovereignty of the Bagrationi depended on the policy of the Mongolian court.

OLAF2NORD.name: Olaf II of Denmark and IV of Norway
OLAF2NORD.summary: Son of Margaret and Haakon VI. He was elected king of Denmark as a child and inherited Norway when his father died. His mother led the government. Olaf's death without descent in 1387 forced another successor solution and opened the way to recognition of Margaret and Erik of Pomerania.

MARIAANABAVFERN2.name: Maria Ana of Bavaria
MARIAANABAVFERN2.summary: Consort of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Their life is linked to Austria, Bavaria.

ADOLFOFEDERICOSUE.name: Adolfo Federico of Sweden
ADOLFOFEDERICOSUE.summary: King of Sweden since 1751, of Holstein-Gottorp's house. He reigned during the era of Freedom, with royal power very limited by the Riksdag.

MARIANAVARRA.name: María de Navarra
MARIANAVARRA.summary: The daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she was the wife of Peter IV of Aragon. Her marriage linked the new ruling Navarren house to the Aragonese monarchy.
MARIANAVARRA.biography: The daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she was the wife of Peter IV of Aragon. Her marriage linked the new ruling Navarren house to the Aragonese monarchy. She died young and her trajectory recalls that the consorts could transmit decisive dynastic connections even if their political life was brief.

PLAISANCEANT.name: Plaisance of Antioch
PLAISANCEANT.summary: Daughter of Bohemond V and wife of Henry I of Cyprus, she served as regent for her son Hugh II. Her presence in Acre shows how Antiochene family alliances also influenced the politics of Jerusalem.

MARGBORGBAV.name: Margarita de Burgundy
MARGBORGBAV.summary: Consort of the Valois-Burgundy dynasty. Their life is linked to Burgundy, Bavaria.

ARNAUDALBRET.name: Arnaud-Amanieu de Albret
ARNAUDALBRET.summary: Lord of Albret in the 14th century, he married Margaret of Bourbon. Her offspring combined the French southwest heritage with ties close to the royal family.
ARNAUDALBRET.biography: Lord of Albret in the 14th century, he married Margaret of Bourbon. His descendants combined the heritage of the French Southwest with ties close to the royal family. He was the father of Charles I of Albret, Constable of France, and occupies a position of link between the lordly origin and the courtly projection of the house.

JUANAFRABRET.name: Joan of France
JUANAFRABRET.summary: Consort of the Valois dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Brittany.

CONST1ARM.name: Constantine I of Cilician Armenia
CONST1ARM.summary: He displaced his brother Smbat and briefly occupied the crown before returning power to Hetum II. His reign was another phase of a dynastic dispute involving several sons of Leo II.

BLANCHAMP.name: Blanche of Champagne
BLANCHAMP.summary: Daughter of Theobaldo I of Navarre and Inés de Beaujeu, she married John I of Brittany. She was the mother of John II. Her position directly connects the Navarre dynasty of Champagne with the Breton dukes and helps to follow the relations between the two regions developed in this update.

ISABELJAGHUN.name: Isabel Jagelón
ISABELJAGHUN.role: Queen consort and Regent of France
ISABELJAGHUN.summary: Consort of the Jagelón dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary, Poland, Transylvania.

MANF3SAL.name: Manfredo III de Saluzzo
MANF3SAL.summary: Saluzzo ruled in the first half of the 13th century, between Savoy's pressures and the alliances with Montferrat. His marriage to Beatriz de Savoy was a union between houses that also rivaled politically.
MANF3SAL.biography: Saluzzo ruled in the first half of the 13th century, between Savoy’s pressures and the alliances with Montferrat. His marriage to Beatriz de Savoy was a union between houses that also rivaled politically. He died leaving Tomás I even less; the tutelage of that generation shows that inheriting the marquisado did not amount to immediately exercising the government.

GOFFREDOBORJA.name: Goffredo Borgia
GOFFREDOBORJA.summary: Prince of the Borja dynasty. Their life is linked to Naples, Squillace.

SOPHIAPALHAN.name: Sofia del Palatinate
SOPHIAPALHAN.summary: The voter of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Palatinate, Hannover.

ISABTIR.name: Isabel of Tyrol
ISABTIR.summary: Consort of the Gorizia dynasty. Their life is linked to Germany, Austria.

MARIAAVES.name: Mary of Hainaut
MARIAAVES.summary: Consort of the Avesnes dynasty. Their life is linked to Bourbon, Hainaut.

CATHPOMNEUMARK.name: Catherine of Pomerania
CATHPOMNEUMARK.summary: Erik’s sister from Pomerania. She married John of the Palatinate-Neumarkt, from the house of Wittelsbach. Her son Christopher was elected in the three Nordic kingdoms after Erik’s fall. Filiation shows family continuity, although Christopher’s access depended on separate choices.

LEONORNAP.name: Leonor of Naples
LEONORNAP.summary: Consort of the Trastámara dynasty. Their life is linked to Ferrara.

SOPHIADOROTHEACELLE.name: Sofia Dorothea de Celle
SOPHIADOROTHEACELLE.summary: Consort of the Welf dynasty, their life is linked to Hanover.

MAGDALENAFRA.name: Magdalene of France
MAGDALENAFRA.summary: Noble of the Valois dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Navarre.

FRED2MEISSEN.name: Frederick II of Meißen
FRED2MEISSEN.summary: Margrave de Meißen, 1323–1349. Margrave of the Wettin dynasty.

MARIAANTONIAAUT.name: Marie Antonia of Austria
MARIAANTONIAAUT.summary: Consort of the Habsburg dynasty. Their life is linked to Austria, Bavaria.

MAGDSIBPRUSSAX.name: Magdalena Sibylla of Prussia
MAGDSIBPRUSSAX.summary: Consort of the Hohenzollern dynasty. Their life is linked to Prussia, Saxony.

JAMES11DESMOND.name: James FitzGerald, XI Earl of Desmond
aliases: James fitz Maurice, 11th Earl of Desmond
JAMES11DESMOND.summary: His rivalry with the Butlers over Munster’s dominance motivated attempts to bring the two houses closer together. His daughter Joan linked Desmond’s heritage with Ormond’s, retaining her own influence between these lineages.

JUANABOR.name: Joan of Bourbon
JUANABOR.summary: Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their life is linked to France.

SANCHACASTAR.name: Sancha de Castilla
SANCHACASTAR.summary: Consort of the Ivrea-Borgoña dynasty. Their life is linked to Aragon, Castile.

TOMAS2SAB.name: Thomas II of Savoy
TOMAS2SAB.summary: Brother of Amadeus IV, he received rights in Piedmont and ruled Flanders for his marriage to Joan. He was not the successor of his father in Savoy County.
TOMAS2SAB.biography: Brother of Amadeus IV, he received rights in Piedmont and ruled Flanders for his marriage to Joan. He was not the successor of his father in Savoy County. His second marriage to Beatriz Fieschi gave rise to the line of Amadeus V; this generation connects the distribution of alpine domains with the subsequent continuance of the Condal.

governmentNotes.Conde de Flandes y Henao por su matrimon: Count of Flanders and Hainaut for his marriage with Countess Juana, till his death.

LUISASAB.name: Luisa de Savoy
LUISASAB.summary: Noble of the Savoy dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Savoy.

BAGRAT7KARTLI.name: Bagrat VII of Kartli
BAGRAT7KARTLI.summary: Raised in the Persian court environment, he was installed by Abbas I after the fall of Luarsab II. His authority depended on the safavid presence and was limited outside the centers that he controlled.

LUDWIG5HESSEDARM.name: Louis V of Hesse-Darmstadt
LUDWIG5HESSEDARM.summary: Landgrave of Hesse-Darmstadt, 1596–1626. Landgrave of the Hesse dynasty.

JOHN1CYPRUS.name: John I of Cyprus
JOHN1CYPRUS.summary: Son of Hugo III, king of Cyprus and titular of Jerusalem since 1284. He died in 1285 after a year of reign and succeeded him by his brother Henry II.

CATALINASUEVASA.name: Catherine of Sweden
CATALINASUEVASA.summary: Daughter of Charles IX and Mary of the Palatinate. Her marriage to Juan Casimiro of the Palatinate-Zweibrücken connected the Vasa with a branch of Wittelsbach. Her son Carlos X Gustavo succeeded Cristina of Sweden: the dynastic name change did not break the family continuity by female line.

JOHANNLUDWIG1ANHALT.name: Juan Luis I de Anhalt-Dornburg
JOHANNLUDWIG1ANHALT.summary: Prince of the Anhalt-Zerbst-Dornburg secondary line, father of Christian Augustus and paternal grandfather of Catherine II of Russia. His dynastic title does not represent a government over all the principalities of Anhalt.

TEIMURAZ1MUKHRANI.name: Teimuraz I of Mukhrani
TEIMURAZ1MUKHRANI.summary: Prince of Mukhrani and father of Vajtang V. He participated in the Georgian resistance to the Safavids and died in Marabda. His son then reached the crown by means of a policy of understanding with Persia.

MARGBORB.name: Margarita de Borbón
MARGBORB.summary: Consort of the Dampierre dynasty. Their life is linked to Navarre, Champagne.

MARIEBLOIS.name: Mary of Blois-Châtillon
MARIEBLOIS.role: Queen consort and Regent of France
MARIEBLOIS.summary: Consort of the Châtillon dynasty. Their life is linked to Anjou, Naples.

STEFANDUSAN.name: Stefan Dušan
STEFANDUSAN.summary: King of Serbia and, since 1346, emperor of Serbs and Greeks. He built the largest medieval Serbian state and promulgated an important legal code, although his empire was fragmented shortly after his death.

ALGIRDASLIT.name: Algirdas
ALGIRDASLIT.summary: He ruled alongside his brother Kęstutis, who dominated Trakai and Western defence. He extended Lithuanian authority over Ruthenian territories, without turning all his principalities and local governments into a uniform administration.

GIORGI3IMER.name: Jorge III de Imereti
GIORGI3IMER.summary: His monarchy lived side by side with the growing strength of Levan II Dadiani of Mingrelia. The clashes between the two limited the crown’s ability to control the Georgian West. His son Alexander III continued that dispute.

ALEXANDER3SCOT.name: Alexander III of Scotland
ALEXANDER3SCOT.summary: His accidental death in 1286 left the Scottish monarchy without a direct adult heir and opened up the great successor crisis of the late 13th century.

JAMES2SCOT.name: James II of Scotland
JAMES2SCOT.summary: King of Scotland from 1437, at age six. He ended the power of the Douglas and died in 1460 when a cannon exploded during the siege of Roxburgh.

MARIAVOICHITAMOLD.name: Maria Voichița
MARIAVOICHITAMOLD.summary: Consort of the Basarab dynasty. Their life is linked to Wallachia, Moldova.

JAMES1SCOT.name: James I of Scotland
JAMES1SCOT.summary: King of Scotland since 1406, he spent eighteen years in captivity in England. Upon his return he reinforced royal authority over the nobility and was assassinated in Perth in 1437.

PHILIPPAENGLAND.name: Philippa of England
PHILIPPAENGLAND.summary: Daughter of Henry IV of England and Mary of Bohun. Her marriage to Erik of Pomerania connected the Lancaster monarchy with Kalmar.
PHILIPPAENGLAND.biography: Daughter of Henry IV of England and Mary of Bohun. Her marriage to Erik of Pomerania connected the monarchy of Lancaster with Kalmar. She participated in the administration and defense of the kingdom during the absences of the king. She died without surviving offspring, so the liaison did not establish a new line of succession.

ANTONIETABORBON.name: Antoinette of Bourbon
ANTONIETABORBON.summary: Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Guise.

CASI3.name: Casimiro III of Poland
CASI3.summary: He strengthened Polish administration and legislation and promoted the foundation of the University of Krakow. He was the last Polish king of the main line of the Piast.

KAIKHOSROKARTLI.name: Kaikhosro of Kartli
KAIKHOSROKARTLI.summary: He received the crown while continuing to serve the safavids outside Georgia. He died during the Kandahar campaign. Vajtang, his brother, administered Kartli, so his title is not represented as a continuous effective government.

HUG4BORG.name: Hugo IV de Burgundy
HUG4BORG.summary: Duke of Burgundy, 1218–1272. Duke of the Burgundy dynasty.

LUISDURAZZO.name: Luis de Durazzo
LUISDURAZZO.summary: Count of Gravina, 1336–1362. Count of the Anjou-Durazzo dynasty.

FERENC2RAK.name: Francis II Rákóczi
FERENC2RAK.summary: The son of Francis I and Jelena Zrinski led the insurrection against the Habsburgs, which began in 1703. His Transylvan election in 1704 and his installation in 1707 were different moments, in the midst of war.
FERENC2RAK.biography: The son of Francis I and Jelena Zrinski led the insurrection against the Habsburgs, which began in 1703. His Transylvan election in 1704 and his installation in 1707 were different moments, in the midst of war. He rejected the Szatmár agreement of 1711 and ended up in Ottoman exile. His title does not imply a continuous dominion of the territory.

governmentNotes.Elección en 1704 e instalación en 1707,: Election in 1704 and installation in 1707, during the war against the Habsburgans; it did not imply continuous control of the entire principality.

CHRISTOPHWURTT.name: Christoph of Württemberg
CHRISTOPHWURTT.summary: Duke of Württemberg who consolidated the Lutheran Reformation and reorganized the duchy institutions. His government gave stability to a branch that had spent decades between dynastic crises and imperial pressure.

LADI1.name: Ladislao I of Poland
LADI1.summary: His coronation in Krakow symbolized the reunification of a significant part of the Polish lands. He fought the Teutonic Order and bequeathed the crown to Casimiro III.

LUARSAB2KARTLI.name: Luarsab II of Kartli
LUARSAB2KARTLI.summary: His reign ended under the pressure of Abbas I, who lured him to Persia and held him captive. He was executed after refusing to convert to Islam. The Georgian Church venerated him as a martyr, linking his memory to the religious defense of the kingdom.

OTTHEINRICHPAL.name: Otto Enrique del Palatinate
OTTHEINRICHPAL.summary: He ruled Pfalz-Neuburg with his brother Philip since 1522 and then alone. In 1556, palatine electoral dignity kept the two principalities separate; Neuburg gave to Wolfgang de Zweibrücken in 1557.

governmentNotes.Gobernó junto a su hermano Felipe; entre: He ruled with his brother Philip and his branches of authority were divided between 1535 and 1541.
governmentNotes.Los estamentos administraron buena parte: The stamina administered a good share of the principality during the financial crisis of 1544-1546.

FRANCOISECHATILLON.name: Françoise de Châtillon
FRANCOISECHATILLON.summary: Wife of Alain de Albret, she was the mother of Juan III of Navarre and Carlota de Albret. Her offspring connect the French nobility heritages with the Navarren monarchy and the Borja. Her birth year is preserved as approximate, avoiding presenting a conventional figure as an exact date.

CRISTINALORENA.name: Cristina de Lorena
CRISTINALORENA.role: Queen consort and Regent of France
CRISTINALORENA.summary: Consort of the Lorraine dynasty. Their life is linked to Lorraine, Tuscany.

GEORGEWILLIAMCELLE.name: George William of Brunswick-Lüneburg
GEORGEWILLIAMCELLE.summary: Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg on Celle’s branch. His daughter Sofia Dorotea linked this line with Hannover, a decisive dynastic connection for the future British succession.

governmentNotes.Gobierno territorial de una rama; no dom: Territorial government by one branch; no exclusive rule over the entire grouping.

GUIL2DAMP.name: William II of Dampierre
GUIL2DAMP.summary: Second husband of Margaret of Flanders and father of Guy of Dampierre. His children competed with those of Margaret’s earlier marriage for the inheritances of Flanders and Hainaut. Their parentage explains why two different houses claimed rights through the same mother.

YOLANDEDREUXSCOT.name: Yolanda de Dreux
YOLANDEDREUXSCOT.summary: A widow of Alexander III of Scotland, she married Arthur II of Brittany. She was the mother of John of Montfort.
YOLANDEDREUXSCOT.biography: A widow of Alexander III of Scotland, she later married Arthur II of Brittany. She was the mother of John of Montfort. Her second marriage originated the branch that would dispute the duchy to the offspring of Arthur's first marriage, while her previous career connected her to the Scottish monarchy.

LUDWIG6HESSEDARM.name: Louis VI of Hesse-Darmstadt
LUDWIG6HESSEDARM.summary: Landgrave of Hesse-Darmstadt, 1661–1678. Landgrave of the Hesse dynasty.

ALBERT7MECK.name: Albert VII of Mecklenburg
ALBERT7MECK.summary: Duke of Mecklenburg, 1503–1547 (branch). Duke of the Mecklenburg dynasty.

governmentNotes.Gobierno territorial de una rama; no dom: Territorial government by one branch; no exclusive rule over the entire grouping.

ALEXANDER2SCOT.name: Alexander II of Scotland
ALEXANDER2SCOT.summary: Son of William the Lion. He reigned from 1214 to 1249 and consolidated the Anglo-Scotish border before dying during a campaign in the west.

PEDRO2SAB.name: Pedro II de Savoy
PEDRO2SAB.summary: Before inheriting the county, he developed an important career in England and gathered his own domains around Lake Leman. His government reinforced controls over Castilians, Revenues and Administration.
PEDRO2SAB.biography: Before inheriting the county, he developed an important career in England and gathered his own domains around Lake Leman. His government reinforced controls over Castilians, income and administration. When he died without a son, the county passed to his brother Felipe; his daughter Beatriz's rights over other estates followed a different trajectory.

PHILIP1POM.name: Philip I of Pomerania
PHILIP1POM.summary: Duke of Pomerania, 1531–1560 (branch). Duke of the Griffin dynasty.

governmentNotes.Gobierno territorial de una rama; no dom: Territorial government by one branch; no exclusive rule over the entire grouping.

ANNABRANDDEN.name: Anne of Brandenburg
ANNABRANDDEN.summary: Consort of the Hohenzollern dynasty. Their life is linked to Brandenburg, Denmark.

ISABARAG.name: Isabel of Aragon
ISABARAG.summary: Consort of the Barcelona dynasty. Their life is linked to France.

JOHNALBERT1MECK.name: Juan Alberto I de Mecklenburg
JOHNALBERT1MECK.summary: Duke of Mecklenburg, 1547–1576 (branch). Duke of the Mecklenburg dynasty.

governmentNotes.Gobierno territorial de una rama; no dom: Territorial government by one branch; no exclusive rule over the entire grouping.

ROB1ART.name: Roberto I de Artois
ROB1ART.summary: Brother of Louis IX, he participated in the Egyptian crusade. He died in Mansura after an offensive that left the French forces in a very compromised situation.

KARL2BADEN.name: Charles II de Baden-Durlach
KARL2BADEN.summary: Margrave of Baden, 1553–1577. Margrave of the Zähringen-Baden dynasty.

ENRIQ16BAV.name: Henry XVI of Bavaria-Landshut
ENRIQ16BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1393–1450 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

RADU1WAL.name: Radu I de Wallachia
RADU1WAL.summary: Voivode of Wallachia, 1377–1383. Voivode of the Basarab dynasty.

ISABVAL.name: Isabel de Valois
ISABVAL.summary: Consort of the Valois dynasty. Their life is linked to Milan, France.

LEVANIMER.name: Levan de Imereti
LEVANIMER.summary: He came to the throne as a teenager and had to face family rebellions and intervention from the neighboring principalities. He was deposed and died captive, leaving open the struggle for control of the Western monarchy.

SOPHIEBRANDSAX.name: Sofia de Brandenburg
SOPHIEBRANDSAX.summary: Consort of the Hohenzollern dynasty. Their life is linked to Brandenburg, Saxony.

ISABELVALOIS1389.name: Isabel de Valois
ISABELVALOIS1389.summary: Consort of the Valois dynasty, their life is linked to France, England.

SIBYLLACLEVES.name: Cléveris's Sibylla
SIBYLLACLEVES.summary: Consort of the La Marck dynasty. Their life is linked to Cleves, Saxony.

FATIMANASR.name: Fatima bint al-Ahmar
FATIMANASR.summary: Princess of the Nasrid dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Granada.

ROD3HAB.name: Rodolfo III of Habsburg
aliases: Rodolfo III de Habsburgo (Rodolfo I de Bohemia)
ROD3HAB.summary: Son of King Albert I of Habsburg. In 1306 he was elected king of Bohemia after the extinction of the Premislids, but died in campaign the following year.

governmentNotes.Autoridad compartida; no se interpreta c: Shared authority; not treated as an exclusive succession.

MARIANAVICT.name: Mariana Victoria of Spain
MARIANAVICT.summary: Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their life is linked to Portugal, Spain.

EBERHARD3DUKEWURTT.name: Eberhard III of Württemberg
EBERHARD3DUKEWURTT.summary: Duke of Württemberg, 1628–1674. Duke of the Württemberg dynasty.

MATIART.name: Matilde de Artois
MATIART.summary: She defended her rights over Artois against the claims of her nephew Robert. Her political position was reinforced by her daughters’ marriages into the French royal family.

BERENGUELANAV.name: Berenguela de Navarra
BERENGUELANAV.summary: Daughter of Sancho VI of Navarre, she married Ricardo I in Limassol (Cyprus) in 1191, during the crusade. She never lived in England; after widowing she lived in Le Mans, which was part of her dowry, and there she founded the Abbey of L’Épau, where she is buried.

GIOVPOPOLANO.name: Giovanni de’ Medici il Popolano
GIOVPOPOLANO.summary: Noble of the Medici dynasty. Their life is linked to Florence.

JOANENGLANDSCOT.name: Joan of England
JOANENGLANDSCOT.summary: Consort of the Plantagenet dynasty. Their life is linked to England, Scotland.

ADELAHOLAVES.name: Adelaide of Holland
ADELAHOLAVES.summary: Sister of William of Holland, she married John of Avesnes. Through her, their son John II was related to the comital house of Holland. That connection proved decisive in 1299, when the death of John I of Holland allowed the inheritances of Holland and Hainaut to be united.

AMALIASAXBAV.name: Amalia of Saxony
AMALIASAXBAV.summary: Consort of the Wettin dynasty. Their life is linked to Bavaria, Saxony.

ANAMARIAORL.name: Ana Maria de Orleans
ANAMARIAORL.summary: Consort of the Bourbon-Orleans dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Savoy.

PIEROILGOTTOSO.name: Piero de’ Medici
PIEROILGOTTOSO.summary: Governor of Florence, 1464–1469. Lord of the Medici dynasty.

GUILLERMO4BAV.name: William IV of Bavaria
GUILLERMO4BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria between 1508 and 1550, initially in dispute with his brother Louis X. In 1516 he promulgated with him the decree on the purity of beer.

CATAPORT.name: Catherine of Portugal
CATAPORT.summary: Infanta of the Avis dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Portugal.

JUANAENR.name: Juana Enríquez
JUANAENR.summary: Daughter of the Admiral of Castile Fadrique Enríquez and Marina de Córdoba, she married John II of Navarre and Aragon and was the mother of Ferdinand the Catholic. During the Catalan Civil War she defended her son’s rights; she died in Tarragona in 1468.

PHILIPPALUXAVES.name: Felipa de Luxembourg
PHILIPPALUXAVES.summary: He married John II of Avesnes and was the mother of William and Mary of Henaus. His offspring linked the county house to England, Bavaria and Bourbon. It should not be confused with his granddaughter Felipa of Hainaut, wife of Edward III.

LUIS2BAV.name: Louis II of Bavaria
LUIS2BAV.summary: Louis the Severus, Duke of Upper Bavaria and Count Palatine of the Rhine. In 1256 he executed his wife Maria de Brabant for a suspicion of adultery; he was a tutor to Conradino.

JOHNFREDWURTT.name: Juan Federico de Württemberg
JOHNFREDWURTT.summary: Duke of Württemberg, 1608–1628. Duke of the Württemberg dynasty.

MARGUERITEBEARN.name: Margarita de Bearne
MARGUERITEBEARN.summary: The daughter of Gaston VII, she contributed the rights to Bearne to the offspring of her marriage to Roger Bernardo III of Foix. Her role is fundamental to understanding the origin of the heritage union.
MARGUERITEBEARN.biography: The daughter of Gaston VII, she contributed the rights to Bearne to the offspring of her marriage to Roger Bernardo III of Foix. Her role is fundamental to understanding the origin of the heritage union. Margarita's birth house and her husband's were different, even though her heirs gathered the titles.

governmentNotes.Titular hereditaria; comparte la continu: Hereditary titleholder; she shared the continuity of the viscounty with her husband and later with her descendants.

ESTEBAN3BAV.name: Stephen III of Bavaria
ESTEBAN3BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1375–1413 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

CATHERINEIVANOVNA.name: Catherine Ivanovna of Russia
CATHERINEIVANOVNA.summary: Duchess of the Romanov dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Russia, Mecklenburg.

JUANCASIMIROPALZWEI.name: Juan Casimiro del Palatinate-Zweibrücken
JUANCASIMIROPALZWEI.summary: Count Palatine of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Their life is linked to Palatinate, Sweden.

LOUISNEVERS.name: Luis de Nevers
LOUISNEVERS.summary: The son of Robert III of Flanders and father of Louis I, died before inheriting the Flemish county. His position allows understanding the leap between grandfather and grandson in 1322. Genealogy preserves this generation even though the succession of Flanders does not include a government of his.

MURAD3OSM.name: Murad III
MURAD3OSM.summary: Sultan of Ottoman Empire, 1574–1595. Sultan of the Osmanli dynasty.

MAURICEHESSEKASS.name: Mauritius of Hesse-Kassel
MAURICEHESSEKASS.summary: Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel, 1592–1627. Landgrave of the Hesse dynasty.

ISABPOM.name: Isabel de Pomerania
ISABPOM.summary: Consort of the Griffin dynasty. Their life is linked to Bohemia, Holy Roman Empire.

ALFPORTINF.name: Alfonso de Portugal
ALFPORTINF.summary: Prince of the Avis dynasty. Their life is linked to Portugal.

JUAN1BRAG.name: Juan I de Braganza
JUAN1BRAG.summary: Duke of the Braganza dynasty. Their life is linked to Portugal.

ISABFRA.name: Isabella of France
ISABFRA.summary: Consort of the Capeto dynasty. Their life is linked to Navarre.

ALF1BRAG.name: Alfonso I de Braganza
ALF1BRAG.summary: Duke of the Braganza dynasty. Their life is linked to Portugal.

BARBARASAXWITTENBERG.name: Barbara de Saxony-Wittenberg
BARBARASAXWITTENBERG.summary: Consort of the Ascania dynasty. Their life is linked to Saxony, Brandenburg.

OTTO1BAV.name: Otto I of Bavaria
OTTO1BAV.summary: Otto de Wittelsbach received the Bavarian Duchy of Frederick Barbarossa in 1180, after the fall of Henry the Lion. His house ruled Bavaria until 1918.

ISABBORG.name: Isabel de Burgundy
ISABBORG.summary: Consort of the Burgundy dynasty. Their life is linked to Germany.

HENRY2NASSAU.name: Henry II of Nassau
HENRY2NASSAU.summary: Earl of Nassau, 1198–1251. Earl of the Nassau dynasty.

ISABLANCASTER.name: Isabel de Lancaster
ISABLANCASTER.summary: Noble of the Plantagenet-Lancaster dynasty. Their life is linked to England.

GEORGE2HESSEDARM.name: George II of Hesse-Darmstadt
GEORGE2HESSEDARM.summary: Landgrave of Hesse-Darmstadt, 1626–1661. Landgrave of the Hesse dynasty.

GUIL4HOL.name: William II of Hainaut
GUIL4HOL.summary: Son of William I of Hainaut, he was also William IV of Holland. He died on campaign in Friesland without legitimate children. His sister Margaret and her children brought the inheritance of the three counties into the Wittelsbach orbit.

ESTEBAN1BAV.name: Stephen I of Bavaria
ESTEBAN1BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1290–1310 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

IVAN2MOSC.name: Ivan II of Moscow
IVAN2MOSC.summary: Great Prince of Russia, 1353–1359. Great Prince of the Rurikida dynasty.

WILLIAM6HESSEKASS.name: William VI of Hesse-Kassel
WILLIAM6HESSEKASS.summary: Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel, 1637–1663. Landgrave of the Hesse dynasty.

ANASWI.name: Anne of Świdnica
ANASWI.summary: Consort of the Piast dynasty. Their life is linked to Bohemia, Holy Roman Empire.

EDUVIGJAGBAV.name: Eduviges Jagelón
EDUVIGJAGBAV.summary: Consort of the Jagelón dynasty. Their life is linked to Poland, Bavaria.

GIULIANOMEDICI1453.name: Giuliano de’ Medici
GIULIANOMEDICI1453.summary: Noble of the Medici dynasty. Their life is linked to Florence.

ANAMARIAHUNBUL.name: Anne Mary of Hungary
ANAMARIAHUNBUL.summary: Consort of the Árpád dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary, Bulgaria.

JUANAFRA1464.name: Joan of France
JUANAFRA1464.summary: Consort of the Valois dynasty. Their life is linked to France.

BOGDAN2MOLD.name: Bogdan II of Moldova
BOGDAN2MOLD.summary: Voivode of Moldova, 1449–1451. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.

LUISEAMALIEBRUN.name: Luisa Amalia of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel
LUISEAMALIEBRUN.summary: Consort of the Welf Dynasty. Their life is linked to Brunswick, Prussia.

BIRGERJARL.name: Birger Jarl
BIRGERJARL.summary: Great Swedish tycoon and regent associated with the consolidation of the monarchy and the expansion of royal power. The dynasty of its descendants would dominate Sweden for generations.

JUANPORT2.name: Juan de Portugal
JUANPORT2.summary: Constable of the Avis dynasty. Their life is linked to Portugal.

JOFREBORJAESC.name: Jofré de Borja and Escriva
JOFREBORJAESC.summary: Noble of the Borja dynasty. Their life is linked to Valencia.

MARGABORG1290.name: Margarita de Burgundy
MARGABORG1290.summary: Consort of the Burgundy dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Navarre.

RALPHNEVILLE1.name: Ralph Neville
RALPHNEVILLE1.summary: First Earl of Westmorland. His marriage to Juana Beaufort linked the Nevilles to the descendants of Juan de Ghent. Among his sons were Ricardo de Salisbury and Cecilia, mother of Edward IV and Richard III.

ANAESTV.name: Anne of Hungary
ANAESTV.summary: Noble of the harp dynasty. Their life is linked to Byzantium.

LUIS8BAV.name: Louis VIII of Bavaria-Ingolstadt
LUIS8BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1443–1445 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

ROB2BORG.name: Roberto II of Burgundy
ROB2BORG.summary: Duke of Burgundy, 1272–1306. Duke of the Burgundy dynasty.

MARIALUXEMBURGO.name: Mary of Luxembourg
MARIALUXEMBURGO.summary: Consort of the Luxembourg dynasty. Their life is linked to France.

JURAJ5ZRIN.name: Juraj V Zrinski
JURAJ5ZRIN.summary: Ban of Croatia between 1622 and 1626, was the son of Juraj IV and father of Nikola VII and Petar IV. His conversion to Catholicism marked the religious politics of his domains. The short duration of his government contrasts with the later projection of his two sons.

GERTHOH.name: Gertrudis of Hohenberg
GERTHOH.summary: Consort of the Hohenberg dynasty, their life is linked to Germany.

LUIS1BAV.name: Louis I of Bavaria
LUIS1BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1183–1231. Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

IVAN6RUS.name: Ivan VI of Russia
IVAN6RUS.summary: Proclaimed Emperor of Russia in 1740 as a baby. Dethroned the following year by Elizabeth, he spent his entire life in prison and died in Schlüsselburg in 1764.

LEOP1AUS.name: Leopold I of Austria
LEOP1AUS.summary: Duke of Austria and Styria, son of Albert I of Habsburg. He supported his brother Frederick in the fight for the German crown and was defeated by the Swiss in Morgarten (1315).

governmentNotes.Gobernó los dominios austríacos junto a: He governed the Austrian lands jointly with his brother Frederick the Fair; his authority was not exclusive.

MATILDEEMPERATRIZ.name: Matilde of England
MATILDEEMPERATRIZ.summary: Daughter of Henry I of England, she married Emperor Henry V and, after being widowed, Geoffrey of Anjou. Named heir by her father, she fought Stephen of Blois in the English civil war known as the Anarchy without ever being crowned, and secured the succession of her son Henry II in 1154.

ALFMOL.name: Alfonso de Molina
ALFMOL.summary: Infant of the Ivrea-Borgoña dynasty. Their life is linked to Castile.

MAGDSIBBAYSAX.name: Magdalena Sibylla of Brandenburg-Bayreuth
MAGDSIBBAYSAX.summary: Consort of the Hohenzollern dynasty. Their life is linked to Saxony.

ESCHIVABEIRUT.name: Eschiva de Ibelin, madame of Beirut
aliases: Eschive of Ibelin, Lady of Beirut
ESCHIVABEIRUT.summary: Heir of the lordship of Beirut, he lost his territorial base with the Mamluk conquest. Married to Guido de Lusignan, he was the mother of Hugo IV of Cyprus. His trajectory connects the loss of continental states with the continuity of their families on the island.

MARGARETAMUSATA.name: Margareta Mușata
MARGARETAMUSATA.summary: Noble of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty. Their life is linked to Moldova.

CONRADMONTJER.name: Conrado de Montferrato
CONRADMONTJER.summary: Marquis of Montferrato who defended Tyre in front of Saladin in 1187. Married to Elizabeth I of Jerusalem and elected king in 1192, he was killed days later.

INGEBORGDIN.name: Ingeborg of Denmark
INGEBORGDIN.summary: Consort of the Estridsen dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Denmark.

SOPHIEMECK.name: Sofia de Mecklenburg
SOPHIEMECK.summary: Consort of the Mecklenburg dynasty. Their life is linked to Saxony.

DOROTHEASOPHIEFARN.name: Dorothea Sofia of Neuburg
DOROTHEASOPHIEFARN.summary: Consort of the Wittelsbach dynasty. Their life is linked to Palatinate, Parma.

LUISABORGIA.name: Luisa Borja
LUISABORGIA.summary: Noble of the Borja dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Romagna.

FELIPE2ORLEANS.name: Philip II of Orleans
FELIPE2ORLEANS.summary: Duke of Orleans, 1701–1723. Duke of the Bourbon-Orleans dynasty.

governmentNotes.Sucesión en el apanage después de Felipe: Succession to the apanage after Philip I; his subsequent position as regent of France does not change the nature of the duchy.

MARGFRAN.name: Margarita de France
MARGFRAN.summary: Consort of the Capeto dynasty. Their life is linked to Brabant, France.

KARLFRIEDRICHBADEN.name: Carlos Federico de Baden
KARLFRIEDRICHBADEN.summary: Margrave of Baden, 1738–1803. Margrave of the Zähringen-Baden dynasty.

governmentNotes.Sucede a su abuelo Carlos III Guillermo: He succeeded his grandfather Charles III William in Baden-Durlach in 1738, under a regency until 1746, and inherited Baden-Baden in 1771. He became elector in 1803 and grand duke in 1806.

GARCIAALVAREZ.name: García Álvarez de Toledo y Carrillo de Toledo
GARCIAALVAREZ.summary: Duke of the Álvarez dynasty of Toledo. Their life is linked to Castile.

JOHNBEAUFORTSOMERSET.name: Juan Beaufort
JOHNBEAUFORTSOMERSET.summary: Duke of Somerset and English commander during the Hundred Years War. His daughter Margarita Beaufort transmitted to Henry Tudor the ancestry of John of Ghent.

TIBBOTBOURKE.name: Tibbot na Long Bourke
TIBBOTBOURKE.summary: The son of Grace O’Malley and Richard Bourke, he maintained family influence through agreements with the Crown. He received the Viscount of May in the 17th century. His career shows the transformation of Gaelic chiefdoms into a nobility titled.

AMICOUR.name: Amicia de Courtenay
AMICOUR.summary: Consort of the Courtenay dynasty, their life is linked to Artois.

TAIRDELBACHCONN.name: Tairdelbach Ua Conchobair
TAIRDELBACHCONN.summary: He expanded Connacht’s power and contested Irish supremacy to other regional dynasties. His sons Ruaidrí and Cathal represent two successive responses to the political change of the 12th century.

JORGE1BAV.name: George of Bavaria-Landshut
JORGE1BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1479–1503 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

GUIL7MON.name: William VII of Montferrat
GUIL7MON.summary: One of the main aleramic marquises, he extended his influence to cities in northern Italy. His daughter Yolanda married Andronic II and took the name Irene.
GUIL7MON.biography: One of the main aleramic marquises, extended its influence through cities in northern Italy. His daughter Yolanda married Andronico II and took the name Irene. When the male line of his house was extinguished, that Byzantine offspring held the rights of Theodoro Paleolologo over Montferrat.

PIETROCOLONNACARD.name: Pietro Colonna
PIETROCOLONNACARD.summary: Cardinal of the Colonna dynasty. Their life is linked to Papal States.

MARIABRABBAV.name: Maria de Brabant
MARIABRABBAV.summary: Consort of the Brabant dynasty. Their life is linked to Bavaria.

ROD1BAV.name: Rodolfo I of the Palatinate
ROD1BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1294–1317 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

ENRIQ15.name: Henry XV of Bavaria
ENRIQ15.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1312–1333 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

GUILLERMO2BEARN.name: William II of Bearne
GUILLERMO2BEARN.summary: The son of Guillermo Ramón, Viscount of Bearne since 1224. He accompanied Jaime I in the conquest of Mallorca and died in the battle of Portopi on 12 September 1229, together with Ramón de Moncada. He was succeeded by his son Gastón VII.

ALESSANDROMEDICI.name: Alessandro de’ Medici
ALESSANDROMEDICI.summary: First Duke of Florence (1532), imposed with the support of Charles V, whose natural daughter Margaret married him. He was murdered in 1537 by his cousin Lorenzino de Medici.

THEODORAWALLBUL.name: Theodora of Wallachia
THEODORAWALLBUL.summary: Consort of the Basarab dynasty. Their life is linked to Wallachia, Bulgaria.

FRED4THUR.name: Frederick IV of Thuringia
FRED4THUR.summary: Landgrave of Thuringia, 1406–1440. Landgrave of the Wettin dynasty.

governmentNotes.La partición distingue Meißen, Osterland: The partition differentiates Meißen, Osterland and Thuringia and the title does not assign all Wettin lands.

STJEPAN1BOS.name: Esteban I Kotroman
STJEPAN1BOS.summary: Ban documented since 1290, ruled at a time of increasing intervention by the Šubićs in Bosnia. He disappeared from the news after the confrontation of 1302. His sons Stephen II and Vladislav lead to two roads of the house: Queen Elizabeth of Hungary and King Tvrtko I.

governmentNotes.Constancia de 1290 y resistencia frente: Constance of 1290 and resistance to Šubić. The end is an approximate cut before 1314 and isn't a date of death.

BELOSLAVABUL.name: Beloslava from Bulgaria
BELOSLAVABUL.summary: Consort of the Asen dynasty. Their life is linked to Bulgaria, Serbia.

ANTONIOBARBERINI_SR.name: Antonio Barberini
ANTONIOBARBERINI_SR.summary: Trader of the Barberini dynasty. Their life is linked to Florence.

ROBERTBRUS5COMP.name: Robert de Brus, V. Mr. de Annandale
ROBERTBRUS5COMP.summary: Lord of Annandale, 1226–1295, Lord of the Bruce Dynasty.

MARGESCOCIA.name: Margaret of Scotland
MARGESCOCIA.summary: Consort of the Estuardo dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Scotland.

FLAVIOCHIGI_SR.name: Flavio Chigi
FLAVIOCHIGI_SR.summary: Noble of the Chigi dynasty. Their life is linked to Siena.

EUDOXIANIZHNY.name: Nizhni Novgorod Eudoxia
EUDOXIANIZHNY.summary: Consort of the Rurikida dynasty. Their life is linked to Russia.

LUIS3BAV.name: Louis III of Bavaria
LUIS3BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria, 1290–1296 (branch). Duke of the Wittelsbach dynasty.

MATILDENASSAU.name: Matilde of Nassau
MATILDENASSAU.summary: Consort of the Nassau dynasty. Their life is linked to Bavaria, Nassau.

MARIAL.name: Maria Láscaris
MARIAL.summary: Consort of the Láscaris dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary.

TAIRDELBACHDONN.name: Tairdelbach Donn O’Brien
TAIRDELBACHDONN.summary: He ruled Thomond and participated in the Irish coalitions against the great magnates. His sons Conor and Murrough inherited different positions: the continuity of Gaelic royalty and the incorporation into the titular nobility of the Tudor.

RODMAN.name: Rodrigo Manrique de Lara
RODMAN.summary: Count of the Manrique de Lara dynasty. Their life is linked to Castile.

MARGARITALUISAORL.name: Margarita Luisa de Orleans
MARGARITALUISAORL.summary: Consort of the Bourbon-Orleans-Gaston dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Tuscany.

CATACERDA.name: Catherine de la Cerda
CATACERDA.summary: Consort of the La Cerda dynasty. Their life is linked to Spain.

ROGER2PALLARS.name: Roger II of Pallars
ROGER2PALLARS.summary: He was the son of Roger I, Count of Pallars Sobirà from 1234 to 1256. He married Sibylla of Berga.

DONOGH2THOM.name: Donogh O’Brien, Count of Thomond
DONOGH2THOM.summary: The son of Conor and Murrough’s nephew, he inherited the county within the agreement with the Tudor monarchy. Opposition from other members of the O’Brien shows the tension between the birthright of the English title and the rights of the Gaelic headship.

INGEBORGERIKSUE.name: Ingeborg Eriksdotter from Sweden
INGEBORGERIKSUE.summary: Noble of the Erik dynasty. Their life is linked to Sweden.

ELIZABETHPRESTON.name: Elizabeth Preston, Duchess of Ormond
ELIZABETHPRESTON.summary: She inherited part of the Ormond estate, and her marriage to James Butler reunited competing family interests. During war, exile and the Restoration she helped protect and recover the family’s property.

CONOROBRIENTHOM.name: Conor O’Brien, king of Thomond
CONOROBRIENTHOM.summary: He succeeded his father Tairdelbach Donn in the Gaelic kingship of Thomond. His brother Murrough replaced him under local succession custom, while his son Donogh would eventually inherit the earldom created by the Tudors.

ARTMACSENIOR.name: Art Mac Murchada
ARTMACSENIOR.summary: King of Leinster of the Kavanagh branch, he sustained the recovery of power of his lineage against Anglo-Norman settlements. His son Art Óg extended that policy and became one of Richard II's main adversaries in Ireland.

BOGDAN1MOLD.name: Bogdan I of Moldova
BOGDAN1MOLD.summary: Voivode of Moldova, 1359–1367. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.

MARGGINEBRASAB.name: Margarita de Ginebra
MARGGINEBRASAB.summary: Consort of the Geneva Dynasty. Their life is linked to Savoy, Geneva.

WILLIAM7CLANRICARDE.name: William Bourke, Earl of Clanricarde
WILLIAM7CLANRICARDE.summary: He belonged to the Burkes branch settled in Connacht. His sons maintained ties to the Jacobite cause; his daughter Honora's marriage to Sarsfield linked the lineage with Irish military exile.

JUANAMAN.name: Juana Manuel de Villena
JUANAMAN.summary: Consort of the Manuel dynasty. Their life is linked to Castile.

LATCUMOLD.name: Lațcu of Moldova
LATCUMOLD.summary: Voivode of Moldova, 1368–1375. Prince of the Bogdan-Mușat dynasty.

TERESAENTENZA.name: Teresa of Entenza
TERESAENTENZA.summary: Countess of Urgel, 1314–1327. Consort of the Entenza dynasty.

MARGRIMANIDOGE.name: Marino Grimani
MARGRIMANIDOGE.summary: Elected doge of the Republic of Venice, 1595–1605. The office was not hereditary; the territories on the map belonged to the Republic.

ARNAUROGER1PALLARS.name: Arnaldo Roger I de Pallars
ARNAUROGER1PALLARS.summary: The son of Roger II, he ruled Pallars from 1256 to 1288. He was tutor to Count Ermengol X of Urgel and rebelled against the Crown in 1275 and 1280; then he served Peter III in the expedition to Tunis in 1282 and in the defense of Ampurdan in 1285.

FRANCISALORENA.name: Francisca de Lorena-Mercoeur
FRANCISALORENA.summary: Consort of the Lorraine dynasty. Their life is linked to Vendôme, Lorraine.

MARIASALVIATI.name: Maria Salviati
MARIASALVIATI.summary: Noble of the Salviati dynasty. Their life is linked to Florence.

JOHNFREDPOM.name: Juan Federico de Pomerania
JOHNFREDPOM.summary: Duke of Pomerania, 1569–1600. Duke of the Griffin dynasty.

ROB1COUR.name: Roberto I
ROB1COUR.summary: Latin Emperor of Constantinople since 1221, from the house of Courtenay. He lost much of his territory to Nicaea and Epirus.

MARIAARKEL.name: Maria de Arkel
MARIAARKEL.summary: Arnold's mother of Egmond, transmitted the family connection with the dukes of the house of Jülich. She died before her son accessed Güeldres. Her place in genealogy allows us to follow hereditary rights through two generations of women.

JOHN1ALENCON.name: Juan I de Alençon
JOHN1ALENCON.summary: Duke of Alençon, 1404–1415. Duke of the Valois-Alençon dynasty.

ADAWARENNE.name: Ada de Warenne
ADAWARENNE.summary: Consort of the Warenne dynasty, their life is linked to Scotland.

WALTERBURGHULSTER.name: Walter de Burgh, Earl of Ulster
WALTERBURGHULSTER.summary: He combined Connacht’s family domains with Ulster County. His expansion confronted him with Gaelic powers and made him one of Ireland’s great magnates. Richard inherited this extensive territorial position.

ELIZABETHBURGHSCOT.name: Isabel de Burgh
ELIZABETHBURGHSCOT.summary: Consort of the Burgh Dynasty. Their life is linked to Scotland, Ireland.

JOHN1BALLIOL.name: Juan Balliol
JOHN1BALLIOL.summary: Elected king in 1292 after Edward I's arbitration in the Great Cause. Deposed in 1296 at the beginning of the open phase of the wars of independence.

VIOLMAN.name: Violante Manuel
VIOLMAN.summary: Consort of the Manuel dynasty. Their life is linked to Castile, Portugal.

MARGOPAVA.name: Margarita de Opava
MARGOPAVA.summary: Consort of the Přemysl-Opava dynasty. Their life is linked to Moravia.

RAYMOND3TRIPOLI.name: Raimundo III of Tripoli
RAYMOND3TRIPOLI.summary: Count of Tripoli and one of the great barons of the kingdom. He acted as regent and was a central figure in the political struggles that preceded Hattin.

FRANCPICC.name: Francesco Piccinino
FRANCPICC.summary: Condotiero of the Piccinino dynasty. Their life is linked to Milan, Naples.

HELENANJOUSER.name: Helena de Anjou
HELENANJOUSER.summary: Consort. Their life is linked to France, Serbia.

MADELEINEAUV.name: Madeleine de la Tour d’Auvergne
MADELEINEAUV.summary: Consort of the Auvergne dynasty. Their life is linked to France, Florence.

TERESAQUIÑONES.name: Teresa Fernández de Quiñones
TERESAQUIÑONES.summary: Noble of the Quiñones dynasty. Their life is linked to Castile.

ANDGRITTIDOGE.name: Andrea Gritti
ANDGRITTIDOGE.summary: Elected doge of the Republic of Venice, 1523–1538. The office was not hereditary; the territories on the map belonged to the Republic.

MARALAZAREVIC.summary: Noble of the Lazarević dynasty. Their life is linked to Serbia.

MARIAKAZIMIERA.name: Maria Casimira de la Grange d’Arquien
MARIAKAZIMIERA.summary: Wife of John III Sobieski and queen of Poland, she influenced court politics and the succession. After the king’s death she lived in Rome and then in France, where she died in 1716.

BIANCADELLAROVERE.name: Bianca della Rovere
BIANCADELLAROVERE.summary: Noble of the Della Rovere dynasty. Their life is linked to Liguria.

GRYZELDAZAM.name: Gryzelda Zamoyska
GRYZELDAZAM.summary: Noble of the Zamoyski dynasty. Their life is linked to Poland.

VIOLANTEBAR.name: Yolande of Bar
VIOLANTEBAR.summary: Consort of the Bar Dynasty. Their life is linked to Aragon.

PAPA_PIO7.name: Pius VII
PAPA_PIO7.summary: Barnabas Chiaramonti, Benedictine born in Cesena in 1742, was elected in Venice in 1800. He signed the concordat with Napoleon (1801), attended his coronation (1804) and was his prisoner between 1809 and 1814; he died in 1823.

governmentNotes.Restauración territorial de 1800; núcleo: Restoration of the Territory of 1600 and the Roman Conservative / Tustius core. Choice 14 March, Coronation 21 March. The occupation of 1809 requires separate condition and does not appear as an effective control.

VAISELGALIT.name: Vaišelga
VAISELGALIT.summary: Son of Mindaugas and Orthodox monk, he regained the government with the help of the Romanovich. In 1267 he gave power to Švarnas and returned to religious life; he died that year.

HENRIETTEMONTB.name: Enriqueta de Montbéliard
HENRIETTEMONTB.summary: Consort of the Montfaucon dynasty. Their life is linked to Montbéliard, Württemberg.

CHARLOTTELAVAL.name: Carlota de Laval
CHARLOTTELAVAL.summary: Noble of the Laval dynasty. Their life is linked to France.

JAKUBSOB.summary: Noble of the Sobieski dynasty. Their life is linked to Poland.

KATARZYNAOPAL.name: Katarzyna Opalińska
KATARZYNAOPAL.summary: Queen Consort of the Opaliński dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Poland.

THOMASPRESTON.name: Thomas Preston
THOMASPRESTON.summary: Veteran of the Spanish armies, returned to Ireland to command the Confederate army of Leinster. His differences with Owen Roe reflect political and military tensions within the Confederation. He ended up in exile after parliamentary advance.

JOHNERNEISOLD.name: Juan Ernesto de Saxony-Eisenach
JOHNERNEISOLD.summary: Duke of Saxony-Coburg-Eisenach, 1572–1595 (co-ruler). Duke of the Wettin dynasty.

PAPA_ALEJANDRO4.name: Alexander IV
PAPA_ALEJANDRO4.summary: Rinaldo dei Conti di Segni, nephew of Gregory IX, was pope between 1254 and 1261. He continued the fight against the Hohenstaufen in the kingdom of Sicily and canonized Saint Clare of Assisi in 1255.

PAPA_CLEMENTE6.name: Clement VI
PAPA_CLEMENTE6.summary: Pierre Roger, Benedictine and chancellor of Philip VI of France, was pope in Avignon between 1342 and 1352. He bought the city from Queen Joan of Naples in 1348 and expanded the palace with a lavish court.

SIBILAFORTIA.name: Sibylla de Fortia
SIBILAFORTIA.summary: Consort of the Fortiá dynasty. Their life is linked to Aragon.

BAYEZID1OSM.name: Bayezid I
BAYEZID1OSM.summary: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, 1389–1402. Sultan of the Osmanli dynasty.

PAPA_GREGORIO11.name: Gregory XI
PAPA_GREGORIO11.summary: Pierre Roger de Beaufort, nephew of Clement VI, was the last pope of Avignon. He moved the court to Rome in 1377, and his death the following year preceded the schism of the West.

RAFFAELLODELLAROVERE.name: Raffaello della Rovere
RAFFAELLODELLAROVERE.summary: Noble of the Della Rovere dynasty. Their life is linked to Liguria.

PAPA_BENEDICTO11.name: Benedict XI
PAPA_BENEDICTO11.summary: Niccolò Boccasini, master general of the Dominicans, was elected in 1303, after the death of Boniface VIII. He raised part of the sentences against Philip IV of France and died in Perugia after eight months of pontificate.

JEREMIWISE.name: Jeremi Wiśniowiecki
JEREMIWISE.summary: Prince of the Wiśniowiecki dynasty. Their life is linked to Poland, Lithuania.

TOMOR.name: Tomasina Morosini
TOMOR.summary: Noble of the Morosini dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary.

MARGROHAN.name: Margarita de Rohan
MARGROHAN.summary: Consort of the Rohan dynasty, their life is linked to France.

JOANAROZ.name: Joan of Rožmital
JOANAROZ.summary: Consort of the Rožmital dynasty. Their life is linked to Bohemia.

PAPA_EUGENIO4.name: Eugenio IV
PAPA_EUGENIO4.summary: Gabriele Condulmer, Venetian and nephew of Gregory XII, was pope between 1431 and 1447. He faced the Basel Council and presided over the ephemeral union with the Greek Church in Florence (1439).

LORENVAL.name: Lourenço Soares de Valadares
LORENVAL.summary: Sir, their life is linked to Portugal.

GABRIELLEESTREES.name: Gabriela de Estrees
GABRIELLEESTREES.summary: Noble of the Estrees dynasty. Their life is linked to France.

PAPA_GREGORIO13.name: Gregory XIII
PAPA_GREGORIO13.summary: Pope known above all for the reform of the calendar that bears his name. He also promoted Catholic education and the strengthening of institutions of the Counter-Reform.

HUMPHREY4TORON.name: Hunfredo IV de Torón
HUMPHREY4TORON.summary: Lord of Toron of the Toron dynasty. Their life is linked to Jerusalem, Toron.

PAPA_INOCENCIO6.name: Innocent VI
PAPA_INOCENCIO6.summary: Étienne Aubert, a Limousin jurist, was pope in Avignon between 1352 and 1362. He sent Cardinal Gil de Albornoz to recover for the Holy See the government of the Pontifical States.

PAPA_GREGORIO15.name: Gregory XV
PAPA_GREGORIO15.summary: Alessandro Ludovisi, from Bologna, was pope between 1621 and 1623. He created the Congregation of Propaganda Fide (1622), regulated the conclave with secret vote and canonized Ignacio de Loyola and Francisco Javier.

PAPA_CLEMENTE10.name: Clement X
PAPA_CLEMENTE10.summary: Emilio Altieri was elected in 1670, at almost eighty years old, and his adopted nephew, Cardinal Paluzzo Altieri, led the government until his death in 1676.

BIANCAL.name: Bianca Lancia d'Agliano
BIANCAL.summary: Noble of the Lancia dynasty. Their life is linked to Sicily.

TRAIDENISLIT.name: Traidenis
TRAIDENISLIT.summary: Grand Duke since 1269 or 1270, defended Lithuania against military orders and regained positions in the Black Ruthenia. His kinship with previous dynasties is not considered proven.

PAPA_URBANO4.name: Urban IV
PAPA_URBANO4.summary: Jacques Pantaléon, son of a shoemaker of Troyes and former Latin patriarch of Jerusalem, was pope between 1261 and 1264. He instituted the feast of Corpus Christi and offered the kingdom of Sicily to Charles of Anjou in front of Manfredo.

PAPA_GREGORIO14.name: Gregory XIV
PAPA_GREGORIO14.summary: Niccolò Sfondrati, bishop of Cremona, was pope between 1590 and 1591. He supported the Catholic League against Henry of Navarre in the wars of religion of France.

CATHHENNEBERG.name: Catherine of Henneberg
CATHHENNEBERG.summary: Consort of the Henneberg dynasty. Their life is linked to Thuringia, Meißen.

PAPA_GREGORIO12.name: Gregory XII
PAPA_GREGORIO12.summary: Angelo Correr, a Venetian, was the Roman pope of the schism between 1406 and 1415. He resigned before the council of Constance to allow the election of Martin V and the end of the schism.
